# C3 origin re-entry: bootstrap routes do not construct their inputs

Date:2026-10-09 (America/Phoenix). Parent d31a9ef0a7b92947e61602cda192aa4d5fb1a016.
Status: OPEN author research decision. No new theorem, impossibility result, independent review or scientific checkpoint closure is claimed.

## The actual frontier
The recent admission and record-transfer results are useful conditional mathematics. They do not establish native acquisition of their inputs. The current proved chain begins with a correctly initialized and accessible global record:

global singleton/pair miss field -> outside-root singleton profile -> exact admission bit -> restricted safe repair policy.

The first arrow is the record-transfer identity; the next is the empty-intersection criterion. Their composition is valid WHEN the global field and template are supplied. The missing connection is from previously justified native input/update objects to an accessible retained field or another sufficient admission certificate. Global moments are one sufficient route, not a necessary representation of every possible solution.

The next research objective therefore remains acquisition/retention, not further algebraic simplification of the decoder or another conditional repair protocol.

## Candidate routes checked against actual sources

| Candidate | What the inspected source permits | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Use the record-transfer producer as an initializer | source(b,c,z) constructs full supports including hidden mask z; produce() sums miss indicators over those full supports before calling decode(m) | Correct offline verification, not acquisition from the observer's available core. No code defect; using it as a native sensor would import the answer-bearing input |
| Initialize by the dynamic residual update law | Updates M from its previous correct value and the named active root's old/new support; source explicitly leaves initial M and observer access unresolved | Does not bootstrap either its own seed or active-support access. Reusing this conditional law is not a derivation of those premises |
| Reconstruct through ordered events | The event-init result requires a legitimate seed plus complete observed event directions; full support reconstruction needs labels and seed supports | Ordered updates alone are not the complete observed ledger. Assuming that ledger simply relocates the missing retained-record input |
| Treat an actual visible successful request as its own certificate | Existing guarded readout allows sound positive certificates after suitable committed edits; its complete relation still includes NOOP for legal requests | A useful conditional observation does not derive guard enforcement, actual outcome resolution or observer access. The earlier internal-record attempt already identifies this distinction; do not count it as a new no-go result |

The complete core-probe relation is a specified set of permitted successors. It is not by itself an implementation of enforcement, an outcome-selection law or a construction of retained observer memory. Conversely, the restricted admitted repair's guard redundancy remains valid; this source finding does not reopen it.

The internal-record attempt already demonstrates why adding "commit every legal request" changes the model. That rule was not adopted here. Neither an external acknowledgment, full-state read, new sensor nor new physical coupling has been inserted.

## Concrete acceptance gate for the next candidate
Name a previously justified native input domain I, with the source of each available field. Then supply:

1. A carrier/record connection identifying where the sufficient information is represented internally, and how its initial correlation with the hidden incidence state is obtained. Defining M from hidden supports is not an accessible initialization map.
2. An action connection showing that the existing native update actually creates or changes that representation under the named request, with allowed versus realized outcomes kept distinct.
3. A retained output that is legitimately available across ordered slices, together with a decoder for the admission predicate. Do not assume that a set of possible records is an actual observed record.
4. An explicit account of initial protected-band knowledge, template/address availability and any complete-palette requirement. Alternative certificate constructions may remove some of these inputs, but must prove that removal.

A candidate may be conditional on inherited native premises, provided those premises really come from the cited construction and are not newly supplied copies of the desired record. Nothing here asserts that quantum registers, global moments or guaranteed progress are necessary for every possible observer. The negative findings apply to the inspected routes only.

## Research decision and evidence
No candidate inspected here closes the input-origin connection. This is a missing mathematical construction, not a permission or API problem. No additional scientific enumeration or Gemini request was launched: there is no new frozen positive mechanism or novel obstruction to test. Repeating the closed transfer/repair campaigns would verify their conditional statements again without addressing this gap.

Eight current source contents, including the index/continuation used for publication, were read at the immutable parent. Their returned Git blob identities were independently recomputed from UTF-8 bytes. The source manifest is evidence/native-record-origin/ORIGIN_REENTRY_SOURCE_CHECK.json. This is source integrity and author reconciliation only; historical execution was not rerun or recertified. No prior proof, review or rejecting control was altered.

The continuation index's fixed aggregate checkpoint count is removed to avoid treating accumulation of scoped results as closure of C3. The individual closeouts remain the authoritative scope/status records. Broad C3 and general C4 remain OPEN. Path A continues; no physical force, fundamental time, inserted geometry, dark matter or GR derivation is introduced.

# C3 native coverage/routing origin — search, coherent-record and Genesis route screen

Date: 2026-10-09 UTC.
Status: OPEN author research note; this candidate shortcut is unsupported by the inspected sources.
Source/parent:248b1cfbdd29063a3806fca5f66d861d356aa897.
This is source reconciliation, not a new theorem, universal obstruction, Gemini acceptance or scientific checkpoint closure. Existing repair closeouts are unchanged.

## Concrete obligation
The closed deficit repair computes a safe coverage certificate from known role incidence patterns and routes actual edits using labelled roots, current pool roles, a known host and committed-edit phase. It does not initialize or make those records accessible.
The question examined here was whether earlier code named native_record_search/native_record_trace, the coherent-record implementation, or a Genesis provenance anchor already supplies that missing input.

## Findings from actual definitions and code

| Inspected route | Actual construction | C3 consequence |
|---|---|---|
| C3 event initialization | Reconstructs a count from a supplied seed and complete valid event directions; reconstructing supports additionally needs event labels and exact seed supports | It is an update theorem, not acquisition of the role template or actual event ledger |
| C3 event-channel result | Distinguishes event occurrence/address from event sign and payload information | An ordered occurrence list alone cannot be promoted into the richer ledger; this is an inherited result, not a new obstruction |
| C3 native-interface result | Extracts information from already initialized full-palette miss counts | Definability from hidden supports is not observer-accessible initialization |
| v15.46 native_record_trace.py | Verifies pinned bytes for a supplied six-qubit demo; returns failure at native joint-state provenance and marks later interfaces unexecuted | It is a static provenance audit, not a native-record generator |
| v15.46 native_record_search.py | Checks five declared source files and their frozen markers; returns no primitive-derived record found in that bounded scope | The function name does not imply an initializer. Its scope explicitly excludes an archive-wide absence claim |
| v15.15 coherent_records.py | initial_joint(rho) inserts a supplied system matrix into a supplied blank register sector; copy_gate constructs controlled copying; encoding requires a supplied compatible schedule | It implements conditional correlations. No map from C3 labelled incidence roots, roles or native edits to those registers/gates is constructed in this source |
| v15.15 actual-record boundary | branch_operator takes a records string; audit enumerates branches and sets actual_record_selected=None | Coherent writing and conditional branch evaluation are distinct from supplying an actual resolved record to this controller |
| v15.09 carrier-origin report | Preserves the missing cross-domain node/site relation; internal structure does not supply that relation | Sorting core roles against register labels would add an unsupported alignment. This report's historical theorem was not re-executed here |
| v15.56 genesis_base.py | Classifies a Genesis Pin as insufficient without certified provenance/lineage/recoverability/repair-compatible descent maps; no shared pin is assumed | Naming a common origin does not construct the C3 initializer or incidence-to-register connection |

The v15.15 construction is a real conditional reversible record implementation, not a defective model. It shows what follows WHEN its carrier, blank registers, copy/control gates and schedules are supplied. It is not legitimate to import those premises as newly derived C3 native machinery.
Likewise the v15.46 audits do exactly their stated job. Their negative provenance flags are not evidence that all possible native record constructions are impossible.

## Candidate disposition
The attempted shortcut “use the existing native-record code to initialize the deficit controller” is not supported. The candidate stops before any incidence-to-register encoding or new actuator/observation rule is adopted.
This is a source-specific failed route assessment. It does not prove that the required interface cannot be derived directly in the incidence system, and it does not assert that quantum machinery is necessary.
No new numerical campaign or Gemini request was issued: there is no new positive construction or novel impossibility theorem here to test. Re-executing the closed repair would test the conditional theorem again rather than answer its input-origin question.

## Exact next construction gate
A future candidate must name an inherited native input I and exhibit:
1. an initialization map or relation producing the required coverage/routing record from I, with each input field's prior source stated;
2. a justified action connection from the named incidence request to the existing native update;
3. a retained result from which the actual edit phase can be tracked, with system-side information kept distinct from observer access;
4. an update preserving the certificate and routing contract through the repair.
For a quantum-register route, the carrier, blank registers, coupling and incidence-to-register map each need their own native derivation. For a direct incidence route, correlated accessible subsystems and their update must actually be constructed. A full-state verifier or a stipulated projection does not supply either.
Do not insert commit-every-legal-request semantics, an external acknowledgment, hidden-state access or a representation chosen to produce the desired answer. Do not repackage the known all-NOOP example as another discovery.

The current blocker is a missing mathematical construction of this connection, not an API outage, a missing permission or a failing repair proof. Broader C3 remains OPEN. The three recent C4 repair results remain scoped CLOSED.

## Source integrity
Eleven source files were read at the immutable parent. Returned blob IDs matched its recursive Git tree; Git blob SHA-1 was independently recomputed from every UTF-8 content. Per-file SHA256 and immutable links are preserved in [the source manifest](evidence/native-record-origin/COVERAGE_ORIGIN_SCREEN.json).
This verifies source identity, not the historical numerical claims. No prior theorem, adverse review, failed run or conditional assumption was modified.
Path A remains active. No physical force, geometry, dark-matter variable, fundamental time or GR derivation is claimed.

# Uniformly safe core writing — scoped obstruction closeout

Date2026-10-09. Status: scoped CLOSED mathematical obstruction; candidate interaction class OBSTRUCTED for the stated initial-record task. Broad C3/C4 remain OPEN.

## Result
The proposed interaction class is OBSTRUCTED for initializing an exact record of an initially hidden predicate: uniformly safe native single-incidence writes, observed only through the complete visible core and transcript-derived memory. This is a scoped mathematical obstruction, not universal observer impossibility or closure of broader C3.

For every named native toggle, projecting after the toggle equals applying the command's known core effect to the old projection. Uniform-before-issue safety makes that same toggle legal in both initially indistinguishable worlds. Induction therefore preserves equal transcripts, memory and stopping decisions. This holds even when core record incidences change and every command commits. It is not the old all-NOOP argument.

The theorem permits core AND hidden writes on arbitrary finite carriers. Its target is the initial hidden predicate, not a necessarily conserved current predicate. In the optional-NOOP relation, every common resolution mask realizes the same visible trace in both worlds, so possible trace languages agree. Probability-law equality requires a common hidden-independent resolution law; arbitrary hidden-dependent kernels are not covered. All-commit is a diagnostic restriction, not a newly derived physical success rule.

The earlier spectator-only result held the core fixed. This result broadens the action/carrier/memory class and treats actual changing core incidences as records. The observation restriction remains load-bearing: unlike the older special carrier's constant-tau output, it does not permit arbitrary tau/cardinality/count observations. On that older carrier those additional outputs were constant, so there is no conflict.

The exact admission pair is an application: both worlds have identical core and protected initial states but opposite outside-intersection predicates. A private observed scratch label can be added and removed safely in both, producing matching nonconstant committed traces. Guarded core-readout remains valid because informative attempts can be unsafe in one initially possible world; state-dependent guard exclusion breaks the common-transition condition.
